messages:
Aisha Patel: Hey team — I pushed a short PRD draft for the 'pool contract' flow (reserved GPU pools). Link: https://redwood.internal/docs/prd/pool-contract-slos-draft.md

Aisha Patel: TL;DR: propose a 3-tier SLO set (Standard / Committed / Enterprise) with explicit throughput floors per pool, canary + proactive scale policy, and a graceful fallback to shared-hosted when capacity is constrained. Need acceptance criteria + edge-case list.

Mike Chen: skimmed. can we put the actual numeric targets up front? saves back-and-forth.

Aisha Patel: yes — added table in the doc. quick copy here:
```
Standard: p95 < 250ms, p99 < 1s, min throughput 50 tok/s per GPU equivalent
Committed: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 400ms, min throughput 200 tok/s per GPU equiv
Enterprise: p95 < 100ms, p99 < 200ms, min throughput 500 tok/s per GPU equiv
```

Lucas Rivera: question: what does "GPU equivalent" map to? v100? a100? need to be explicit for customers signing contracts.

Aisha Patel: good call — doc now maps to normalized units: 1 GPU equiv = A100-40GB baseline. we also include conversion table for A10g, T4, etc.

Tara O'Neil: acceptance criteria suggestion: 1) canary runs 1% traffic for 72h with no >2x error spike; 2) autoscale reaction time validated under synthetic ramp; 3) fallback to hosted returns responses within 2x latency of baseline and annotated in logs.

Mike Chen: +1 on canary. also add token-accuracy regression check for top customer prompt set (we have eval harness). If model change alters output distribution > threshold, block rollout.

Oliver Grant: operational edge case: what if a customer's reserved pool saturates but other pools are idle due to placement constraints? do we allow cross-pool borrowing? what's the contract language?

Aisha Patel: thinking: soft-borrow allowed in emergency with auto-notify + billing credit; hard-borrow only via manual escalation. add as edge-case and to launch checklist.

Lucas Rivera: autoscale policy detail: hysteresis to avoid flapping. propose: scale-up when sustained 85% util for 60s, scale-down when <40% for 10m. keep max burst window of 5m.

InfraBot: Deploy note: Autoscaler v2 supports policy knobs: min_replica, max_replica, scale_up_threshold, scale_down_threshold, stabilization_window_seconds. Use `infra/autoscaler-v2/2026-03` config.

Tara O'Neil: test plan items: - synthetic OC load to validate throughput floors - chaos test: kill 1/3 GPUs in a zone, validate fallback and no customer impact beyond SLO degradation guardrails - billing smoke to confirm credits applied on soft-borrow

Mike Chen: edge-case: long-running KV-cache heavy sessions blow up memory and reduce throughput. Add explicit session limits and an eviction policy requirement.

Aisha Patel: added session limits: max 60k tokens cached per request by default, configurable with warn at 40k. eviction policy doc link added.

Oliver Grant: rollout plan: 1) internal alpha (eng teams + 2 pilot customers) 2) open beta (select customers with contracts) 3) GA. Add rollback triggers: >3% customer error rate for 30m or p99 latency >2x target for 30m.

Lucas Rivera: can we automate the rollback? yes but require manual confirmation for Enterprise tier.

Tara O'Neil: acceptance criteria checklist draft: - KPI smoke: latency & throughput floors met in canary for 72h - Regression: prompt-set eval within threshold - Observability: trace and cost dashboards wired - Playbook: runbook + escalation + billing flow tested

Aisha Patel: awesome. next steps: please leave line comments in the doc by EOD Thursday. I'll consolidate and send to legal/product ops for contract language by Friday. :thumbsup:

Mike Chen: left comments on the numeric floors and the conversion table.

InfraBot: Reminder: scheduled infra freeze on 2312353600 - if canary spans that window, coordinate oncall.

Oliver Grant: noted. I'll coordinate with infra.

Aisha Patel: thanks everyone — huge help. I'll post the final PRD + acceptance checklist after consolidation.
